chapter_title: Concerning the Wheel that exists in front of the K

1.original: [of the King of Honour who dwells in]
1.content: of the King of Honour who dwells in

spiritual_reading:
Again the teaching speaks about the total ordering of the outermost degree that stands openly before the Divine, within the highest heaven, as the first containment and fastening of all subordinate governing principles in both higher and lower regions, held in a severe restraint; for the whole determination of the Divine rule is fixed there as the governing ultimate. Moreover, every hostile impulse and resisting intention that arises within the heavens is gathered, confined, and held fast within that same restraint.

This ultimate ordering is in the brightness of manifest wisdom, arranged with harmonious form and the appearance of perfect order. Within it is the full completeness of discriminations that keep distinct each heaven and each governing power within it; and all of them are held within that discrimination, so that if any governing principle should attempt to withdraw from its appointed order, it is immediately constrained. If it should attempt to introduce a hidden perversion within its constraint, that perversion becomes at once evident and is known within that ordering. All general knowledges in externals, all distinct knowledges within them, and the chief directing influence among operative powers are present there and are made knowable by means of that ordering, in the Divine presence.

The fullness of discrimination within that ordering includes a sufficient complement of bright operative powers conjoined and mutually intertwined throughout the whole extension of the outermost degree; and every state in which they are pressed into limitation, and every state in which they are given freedom of extension, is laid open by that same ordering. For the first basis of all the heavens above and below, and of their governing powers, is held, fixed, and made immovable within it.

A perpetual attentive discernment is maintained directly before the Divine, so that a holy dread—rising from the Divine presence—seizes all composite and mixed operative forces, and keeps their first principles fastened there, so that they cannot withdraw from the restraint that binds them into order.

In this respect that ultimate ordering is like a tight and unbroken restraint before the protecting vigilance that guards the Divine order; for whenever anything stirs toward disorder among those held within the restraint, the disturbance is immediately within that vigilance.

This is likewise the case for all governing principles in the heavens, and for every operative force in the outermost degree: if any should attempt to withdraw, it is at once identified and uncovered by that ordering. For this ordering is as an all-disclosing faculty of discernment, because the power to distinguish and reveal every quality and tendency is present within it.

fills.notes: The oldest layer introduces sections with the impersonal didactic voice: ‘Again the teaching speaks…’, matching the spiritual translation’s ‘Again the teaching speaks…’.

fills.fill: of the King of Honour who dwells in
fills.notes: Fits the substrate cosmology where the King of Honour stands at the summit (seventh firmament) and the ‘wheel’ is positioned before him as an ultimate restraint and disclosure.
The phrase needs a local adverbial completion: the wheel exists ‘in front … in the seventh firmament there’, i.e., fixed in the highest outermost boundary.
Correspondentially, hostile impulses are not merely ‘in’ the restraint but collected into it, then held fast (‘ensnared’ follows). ‘Gathered’ matches the spiritual translation’s ‘gathered, confined’.
The seals function as discriminations and constraints between each firmament and its rulers. The text immediately explains: they are ‘in it; for should one… wish to escape, he will be bound…’.
Completes the conditional: if a ruler wishes to escape, he will be bound ‘there’, i.e., by the wheel’s present constraint before the King of Honour.
Old-layer register prefers direct manifestation: any attempted trick ‘will be apparent’, not moralized. This matches the spiritual translation’s ‘becomes at once evident’.
The disclosure is immediate and internal to the ordering: the trick is known ‘in that wheel itself’, matching the spiritual translation’s ‘known within that ordering’.
The sentence concerns the perpetual ‘observation’ stationed opposite the King; specifying ‘of the wheel’ keeps the focus on the same ultimate instrument of disclosure and restraint.
Restores the fixed throne-setting of the King of Honour without devotional overlay; ‘in his place’ expresses the stable Divine presence before which the observation stands.
Correspondentially the ‘fear’ is not terror but awe proceeding from the Divine presence; thus it ‘is from him’, matching the spiritual translation’s ‘rising from the Divine presence’.
The fear seizes the mixed powers and also maintains their fastening; ‘and will hold’ supplies the operative continuation leading to ‘their root affixed there’.

The simile needs the trigger-condition: whenever any motion toward disorder occurs among those restrained, it is immediately detected—matching the spiritual translation’s ‘whenever anything stirs toward disorder’.
The referent is the restrained rulers and powers under vigilance. ‘Guarded’ keeps the impersonal custodial register (chief guard) rather than moralized ‘saved’.
Completes the repeated image: wheel resembles a chain; later clause refers to ‘in the … in the chain’.

Restores the clause ‘the discrimination of all things is set in it’, i.e., the distinguishing faculty is established within the wheel, aligning with the spiritual translation’s ‘power to distinguish… is present within it’.

assessment: Most gaps are recoverable because the chapter is structurally repetitive: the ‘wheel’ is the ultimate restraint and disclosure before the King of Honour; the ‘seals’ are discriminative constraints; attempted escape or hidden perversion becomes immediately manifest. Where only a locative or brief connective was missing (e.g., ‘there’, ‘itself’), restorations are tight. A few fills remain moderate because the exact adverbial wording is not uniquely forced, but the correspondential function (immediate manifestation within the ultimate ordering) strongly constrains the sense.
